I will keep to the crop pattern I trust most here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That is what fits our weather, my age, and the way I know how to farm. I do not want a crop that needs too much hand work or carries too much market risk. Wheat and maize are familiar, easy to sell, and match our local water and fertilizer habits. At the start of this growing season, I would already have winter wheat in the field from last autumn, so my first job is to manage that wheat well through spring with one topdressing, a few irrigations if water allows, and disease and weed control when needed. After wheat harvest, I will quickly sow summer maize to catch the heat and rains. I will use improved or hybrid seed because it gives me steadier yield, and I will keep fertilizer at moderate levels to control cost. I prefer rotary tillage because it is practical and common for me, and it lets me turn the land around fast between wheat harvest and maize planting.
